name: British Virgin Islands
season: Peak season runs from mid-December to April. June to November is hurricane season, when prices drop and some weeks need flexible plans.
summary: Short, line-of-sight hops between more than 50 islands make the BVI the easiest bareboat area in the world, and the home of our own catamaran.
highlights: Jost Van Dyke and White Bay

name: Bahamas
season: Winter and spring bring steady trade winds and the clearest water. Summer is hotter, calmer and cheaper.
summary: Shallow turquoise banks, empty cays and swimming pigs. Catamarans are ideal here because of their shallow draft.
highlights: Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park

name: St. Martin and Anguilla
season: Best from mid-December to April. Hurricane season runs June to November.
summary: French and Dutch food culture, long crossings to St. Barths and Anguilla's white beaches, for sailors who want a bit more open water.

name: Grenada and the Grenadines
season: Dry season runs December to June. Grenada sits at the south of the hurricane belt.
summary: Unspoilt islands, the Tobago Cays marine park and a more adventurous feel than the Virgin Islands.

name: Greece
season: May, June and September are ideal. July and August are busiest; the Aegean's meltemi wind can be strong then, so the Ionian suits families.
summary: Thousands of islands, from the sheltered Ionian to the Cyclades. Great food, ancient sites and short day sails.

name: Croatia
season: June and September balance warm water and fewer crowds. July and August are peak and book early.
summary: The Dalmatian coast's islands, walled towns and national parks, with the biggest charter fleets in Europe.
